questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by an adult.
Will be safe standing on the floor in the back.
Will not get hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand in the vehicle while it is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand in the vehicle while it is moving.
questions.explanation: Child safety seats are made for small children. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during a crash or sudden stop. Always use a proper safety seat for children.

questions.question: You enter a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. You should:

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels left to get ready to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Start signaling about 100 feet before you turn left. Keep your wheels pointing straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another car hits you from behind.

questions.question: At night, an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on and blinds you. You should:

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane. Watch the oncoming car from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Does not increase crash risk.
Gives you more time to react to danger.
Often causes risky driving choices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often causes risky driving choices.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to poor driving decisions.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
Keep your normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down when entering a work zone. Follow posted speed limits. Watch for workers and be prepared to stop suddenly.

questions.question: If traffic is moving across railroad tracks, it is safe to stop on the tracks for a short time.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Never stop on railroad tracks. Before crossing, make sure your whole vehicle will fit on the other side.

questions.question: When merging onto a highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Cross two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: Find a gap wide enough for your vehicle to enter safely. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless you cannot find a safe gap.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle:

options.text: On a hill or curve because few cars are coming.
By driving on the road shoulder.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Do not drive on the shoulder to pass. Do not cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: On a road with multiple lanes, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: No one can pass.
Both directions can pass.
Only the side with the dashed line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only the side with the dashed line can pass.
questions.explanation: When one line is solid and one is dashed, only the driver next to the dashed line may pass. The driver next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means:

options.text: Both directions can pass.
The side with the broken line can pass.
The side with the solid line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The side with the broken line can pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you may pass.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to see you and stay out of your way.
Drive very close to the parked cars to give more room to moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your car and parked vehicles. A person may step out of a parked car without looking. A driver may start moving their car before they see you.

questions.question: When driving on icy or snowy roads, what helps prevent crashes?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better grip.
Leave highways as quickly as possible.
Use four-wheel drive.
Drive slower and stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower and stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snowy or icy roads. Reducing your speed and increasing your distance from other cars are the best ways to avoid crashes in these conditions.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign means:

options.text: Watch for existing or possible hazards.
A school zone is ahead.
A public recreation area is ahead.
Food and gas are coming up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for existing or possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers about hazards on the road. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means the light will soon turn red. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Keep going and leave the intersection safely.
Speed up so you don't cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going and leave the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, drive through safely and quickly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You cannot turn left here.
You can turn left only after you stop.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn left here.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign means no left turns.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:

options.text: Braking too much.
Braking suddenly.
Turning suddenly.
Driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast, your tires cannot push water away from the road. They lose grip and slide on the water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other cars?

options.text: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes, it is good defensive driving.
Yes, it is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you drive so slowly that you block normal traffic, you can get a ticket.

questions.question: When can you drive on the right shoulder of the road?

options.text: Only when a police officer or official tells you to.
When the car in front of you is driving too slowly.
When the car in front of you is turning.
When the shoulder is paved.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only when a police officer or official tells you to.
questions.explanation: You can only drive on the shoulder if an official directs you to do so. Do not pass another car on the right shoulder unless it is legal and safe.

questions.question: If your tires lose contact with the road, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear to slow down.
Release the gas pedal gently.
Pump the brakes hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal gently.
questions.explanation: If your tires lose grip, ease off the gas and avoid braking. Do not try to stop or turn until your tires grip the road again.

questions.question: When turning left, you must let right-of-way go to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Cars coming toward you.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming cars. Also always yield to pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must:

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are driving.
Stop only if you are driving in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are driving.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when you see a school bus picking up or dropping off children. This is true no matter which direction you are driving.

questions.question: In rainy weather, you should be most careful when turning or stopping:

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after the rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars mixes with the rain and makes the road very slippery.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway is starting.
A steep hill is ahead.
The overpass ahead is low.
Two lanes of traffic going opposite directions are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead is low.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the overpass ahead is low. Do not go under it if your vehicle is taller than the height shown (13 feet, 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: When driving on a slippery surface, such as snow or ice:

options.text: Use a low gear before driving down steep hills.
Follow other vehicles closely to keep traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a low gear before driving down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Use a low gear before going down a steep hill to prevent skidding. Stay farther back from other vehicles than normal. Avoid sudden stops. Pump your brakes to slow down unless your car has antilock brakes.

questions.question: If a driver sees an animal on the roadway:

options.text: No special action is needed.
The driver should honk the horn.
The driver should pass the animal as close as possible.
The driver should be very cautious.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver should be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when you see an animal on the road. Pass the animal slowly to avoid scaring it.
